name: light_curve_r_dra
notes: R Draconis saturates SPHEREx at every wavelength measured, so its brightness is the flux in an annulus 7-11 px around it (PSF wings), which is a fixed fraction of the total only at one wavelength and detector position.

flux is relative: each point divided by the fitted mean level of its own wavelength bin (0.5% wide, per detector), so points from different wavelengths can share one curve. flux_err includes a 2% calibration floor.
Detectors 1, 2, 3 (0.75-2.42 um); only wavelength bins seen at two or more epochs over 30 days apart are used.

Model: ln F = bin level + per-detector sinusoid with a common period and phase. Points more than 4x the robust residual scatter from the model are marked outlier and left out of the fit; period_err_days is scaled by the reduced chi^2.

Reduced chi^2 of the best fit: 279.5: the wing fluxes scatter much more than their photon noise (exposures minutes apart in the same band can differ by tens of percent), so the curve shows the trend, not small wiggles.
The SPHEREx data span 426 days, 1.7 cycles of the literature period: enough to see the star vary, too short to pin a period down.

The best period moves between 207 and 287 days when the wavelength bins change (0.2%, 0.5%, 1.0%, 2.0%); that spread, not period_err_days, is the honest uncertainty. The literature period (~245 d) lies inside it.
